name: Gregor Muller
profile: Austrian entrepreneur who co-founded online/hybrid tutoring platform GoStudent in Vienna in 2016 with CEO Felix Ohswald. GoStudent has raised over EUR 675m (Prosus, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Left Lane) at a peak valuation around EUR 3bn, and has expanded via acquisitions (Seneca Learning, Tus Media, Studienkreis, Berlitz Germany sites).
interesting_fact: GoStudent Group reported its first full year of operational profitability in 2025, after a period of rapid post-pandemic expansion and restructuring.
deep_cut_fact: Before it was a platform, GoStudent began in 2016 as a WhatsApp chat through which pupils could go over their homework with tutors.
notes: Common name: a different Gregor Mueller (health economist, Thieme RECOM) exists - don't confuse. Lower public profile than CEO Felix Ohswald; GoStudent press office is best route.

name: Ben Christensen
profile: Michigan Tech alum ('14) who co-founded Handshake, the college-to-career recruiting network, with Garrett Lord and Scott Ringwelski in Houghton, Michigan. Handshake now connects ~20M students and alumni with 1M+ employers (valued ~$3.5bn) and has pushed into supplying expert talent for AI training work.
interesting_fact: Christensen nearly took a cybersecurity job at a Michigan company instead; the founders gave themselves three years to sign five schools or give up.
deep_cut_fact: He met Garrett Lord in a Michigan Tech outdoor adventure group; on early sales trips they often slept in a Ford Focus in McDonald's parking lots and once drove to Virginia and back for a single school visit.
notes: Low-profile co-founder (Crunchbase lists Denver base; previously Arbor Networks ASERT security research). Press office or Michigan Tech alumni connection are natural routes.

name: Charles Hearn
profile: Engineer who co-founded Alloy in 2015 with Tommy Nicholas and Laura Spiekerman; Alloy's identity-decisioning and fraud-prevention platform connects banks and fintechs to KYC/AML data sources and is used by 900+ financial institutions. As CTO he built the platform on AWS and still leads engineering.
interesting_fact: Named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2020; Alloy's platform architecture he led has been profiled by AWS Startups.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alloy he was a program manager at Microsoft and then lead product engineer at a payments startup (a high-risk payment processor), where he first met his future co-founders.
notes: Technical, low-profile co-founder; Alloy comms (Kylee Sibilia, listed as media contact on press releases) is the route.

name: Renato Andrade
current_role: Co-founder, Merama; reportedly CEO of Omniteca since 2025 (directory listing only, unverified)
profile: Brazilian ex-McKinsey consultant (USP business degree, INSEAD MBA) who co-founded Merama in Dec 2020 with Guilherme Nosralla and others. Merama buys majority stakes in independent brands selling on Amazon/Mercado Libre across Latin America and became a unicorn in Dec 2021 at a $1.2bn valuation after Advent and SoftBank-backed rounds.
interesting_fact: Merama reached unicorn status less than a year after founding, with a $60m Series B extension valuing it at US$1.2bn.
deep_cut_fact: He and Nosralla met at McKinsey (Renato spent 5+ years there serving retail/consumer clients); the Merama idea came after they read about a funding round for US brand aggregator Perch and found nothing similar in Latin America.
notes: Current role uncertain: theofficialboard.com lists him as CEO of Omniteca (joined 2025) - verify via LinkedIn before outreach. Common name in Brazil; match via Merama/McKinsey/INSEAD. No published direct contact found.

name: Kyle Porter
current_role: Founder and board member/former chairman, Salesloft (now merged with Clari); LP at Stage 2 Capital
profile: Atlanta entrepreneur who co-founded sales-engagement platform Salesloft in 2011 out of Georgia Tech's ATDC and led it as CEO through Vista Equity's ~$2.3bn acquisition (2021). He stepped down as CEO in 2023 (David Obrand succeeded him) and stayed on the board; Salesloft agreed to merge with Clari in 2025.
interesting_fact: Porter insisted Salesloft stay an 'Atlanta unicorn', refusing investor pressure to relocate; early culture perks included rotating a Porsche 911 to the top sales rep each month.
deep_cut_fact: Salesloft killed its original, most profitable product, the lead-scraping tool Prospector, because customers were using it for spam, betting the company on Cadence, then a tiny ~$75k business, which became the flagship.
notes: Active in Atlanta startup ecosystem (Endeavor Atlanta board per directories) and appears on podcasts; LinkedIn is the most direct published route.

name: Elram Goren
current_role: Co-founder, Fabric (Get Fabric); former CEO (stepped down 2022) - current role not publicly confirmed
profile: Israeli entrepreneur and former IDF intelligence-technology officer who co-founded CommonSense Robotics in 2015 with Ori Avraham and Shay Cohen; it rebranded as Fabric in 2019, moved HQ to New York, and raised hundreds of millions for robotic micro-fulfillment centers for grocers and retailers (partners incl. Instacart, Super-Pharm, Walmart).
interesting_fact: Fabric's pitch was a 'third option' for retailers: robotic micro-fulfillment hubs close to customers so on-demand delivery doesn't require loss-making unit economics.
deep_cut_fact: Fabric started life as CommonSense Robotics; asked in a 2021 Calcalist '20-Minute Leaders' interview for three words to describe himself, Goren answered: 'Yes, we can.'
notes: Replaced as CEO by COO Jack Jacoby in July 2022 restructuring (said to remain with the company); no public info on his current activity. No published direct contact found.

name: Dan Cogan-Drew
profile: Former teacher and charter-school digital-learning director who co-founded Newsela with Matthew Gross in 2013. Newsela began by rewriting news articles at multiple reading levels for classrooms and grew into a K-12 content platform (later adding Formative) used by millions of educators; he leads its academic work on student outcomes.
interesting_fact: Newsela 'started with news content, differentiated for students' - the same article published at several reading levels so a whole class could read it together.
deep_cut_fact: He began his education career in Teach For America and went on to teach in public and private schools - and in the U.S. Navy; he holds degrees from Wesleyan, Brown and Tufts.
notes: Educator-first founder; frequent speaker (ASU+GSV, ASCD). Newsela press office is the published route.

name: Diego Torres Martins
current_role: Founder & CEO, unico (unico IDtech), HQ moved to Menlo Park in 2026
profile: Brazilian founder of unico, a digital-identity/biometric verification company processing tens of millions of authentications a month for banks, fintechs and retailers. Valued at ~$2.6bn after SoftBank, General Atlantic and Goldman Sachs rounds; he briefly moved to global CTO (2024), returned as CEO in 2025, and in 2026 relocated HQ to Silicon Valley to expand globally.
interesting_fact: In 2026 unico moved its headquarters from Brazil to Menlo Park, California, after acquisitions in Mexico, the UAE and the US (incl. passwordless-identity startup OwnID).
deep_cut_fact: About 12 years before GA invested, Martins was mentored via Endeavor by General Atlantic's Martin Escobari, who told him the business wouldn't work; Martins asked if he could come back every six months to pitch again - GA later backed unico.
notes: Active in Endeavor/Davos circles; often quoted in Brazilian business press. No published press email found on unico.io.

name: Jouk Pleiter
profile: Dutch software entrepreneur (MSc, University of Groningen) who earlier co-founded web content management vendor Tridion (later SDL Tridion), then founded Backbase in 2003. Backbase's engagement-banking platform is used by 100+ banks worldwide; it bootstrapped for ~16 years before a 2019 Motive Partners investment valuing it around EUR 2.5bn.
interesting_fact: Backbase stayed bootstrapped for almost two decades, growing from services revenue to a global banking-software vendor before taking significant outside capital.
deep_cut_fact: To fund the core product in its early, bootstrapped years, Backbase took on side projects such as building websites for beer companies - anything to bring in cash to reinvest.
notes: Frequent conference speaker and podcast guest (Fintech Leaders, Oliver Wyman Innovators Exchange); Backbase PR is the published route.

name: Gil Mandelzis
profile: Israeli-born serial fintech founder. He founded post-trade processing firm Traiana in 2000 and sold it to ICAP for $250m in 2007, then ran ICAP's EBS BrokerTec FX and fixed-income electronic markets business. In 2017 he founded Capitolis, a capital-markets technology firm (capital marketplace, portfolio optimization, eSecLending) that helps banks free up balance sheet.
interesting_fact: Goldman Sachs named him one of its 'Most Exceptional Entrepreneurs' of 2025 at its Builders and Innovators Summit in Healdsburg, California.
deep_cut_fact: His first company, Traiana, became the subject of a Kellogg School of Management business case study after its growth from a small start-up to a global post-trade leader.

public_contacts.value: Media Relations contact listed on Capitolis press releases (email obfuscated on page)

notes: Capitolis Media Relations email appears on press releases but is hidden by email obfuscation; check the release in a browser. Studied at Tel Aviv University.

name: Thomas Jermoluk
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Beyond Identity (CEO is now Jasson Casey)
profile: Veteran tech executive ('TJ'): Bell Labs and HP engineer, then president/COO of Silicon Graphics (1992-96), founding chairman & CEO of broadband pioneer @Home (led the 1999 Excite merger), and a Kleiner Perkins general partner. In 2020 he co-founded passwordless-authentication company Beyond Identity with Jim Clark, serving as CEO before handing over to Jasson Casey.
interesting_fact: At SGI he oversaw 11,000+ employees and drove deals including the MIPS and Cray Research acquisitions; he and Netscape founder Jim Clark reunited to launch Beyond Identity with $30m Series A.
deep_cut_fact: A self-described 'original nighttime hacker', he got into computing in Hawaii when his 11th-grade math teacher had him writing programs on rented computer time, then joined the night-owl computer culture in Virginia Tech's McBryde Hall (CS '78, MS '79).
notes: Long-time Silicon Valley figure, Virginia Tech alumnus. No published personal or press email found; route via Beyond Identity.

name: Orlando B. Vea
current_role: Founder of Voyager Innovations / Maya (Maya Innovations Holdings); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Filipino telecom and fintech entrepreneur ('Doy'). He co-founded Smart Communications in 1991 with Dave Fernando and was its president/CEO until 2000, later returning as Chief Wireless Advisor. In 2013 he led the formation of Voyager Innovations, PLDT/Smart's digital unit, whose PayMaya became Maya, now one of the Philippines' leading digital banks/e-wallets (KKR, Tencent, IFC backed).
interesting_fact: His stated mission with Voyager/PayMaya was to serve the 'financially underserved' - at the time about 77% of Filipino adults had no bank account while 86% had internet access.
deep_cut_fact: An electrical engineering graduate of the University of the Philippines, he co-founded Smart eMoney with Manuel V. Pangilinan - the entity that was later rebranded PayMaya and is now Maya.
notes: Current formal role at Maya unclear (sources are dated; Shailesh Baidwan is Maya Group President). Low public profile; no published direct contact found.

name: Alexandre Perez Casares
current_role: Co-founder, Fever (live-entertainment discovery and ticketing platform), London-based
profile: Spanish co-founder of Fever, launched in 2014 with Ignacio Bachiller and Francisco Hein. Fever uses data to create and sell live experiences (e.g. Candlelight concerts, immersive exhibitions) in 100+ cities and reached unicorn status (~$2bn) with backing from investors incl. Goldman Sachs and Atomico. Stanford MBA and Harvard Kennedy School MPA; ex-McKinsey.
interesting_fact: Fever's signature Candlelight concert series - classical and pop music performed by candlelight in unusual venues - now runs in cities from Raleigh and Washington DC to Kagoshima, Japan.
deep_cut_fact: Besides his business degrees, he is a trained music professor from the Conservatory of Music of Salamanca, and has served as president of the Altius Society in Oxford, a non-profit studying technology's impact on society.
notes: Deep-cut fact rests on a single TheOrg profile - confirm before using. Lower profile than CEO Ignacio Bachiller; Fever press department is the route.

name: V.R. Govindarajan
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Chairman, Perfios Software Solutions (Bengaluru)
profile: Indian software entrepreneur (IISc Bangalore engineering; MS in CS in the US; database work at DEC and IBM) who co-founded IT product-engineering firm Aztecsoft, sold to MindTree in 2008. With Debasish Chakraborty he then founded Perfios, which pivoted from consumer personal-finance software to B2B credit-underwriting and financial-data analytics for banks and became a unicorn after a 2022 Warburg Pincus-led round.
interesting_fact: Perfios started as a web-based personal finance management tool for retail consumers before pivoting to serve lenders; today its software can read data from 250+ financial institutions and returns credit decisions in under a minute.
deep_cut_fact: He became a founder back in the 1980s, when it was unusual for trained engineers in India to enter the start-up space; years later Perfios was fielding unexpected enquiries from recruitment portals, healthcare firms and even matrimony services.
notes: Perfios CEO is now Sabyasachi Goswami; Govindarajan is executive chairman. Only a general company inbox is published.

name: Tom Feldman
profile: Rocket engineer who co-founded Stoke Space in 2020 with CEO Andy Lapsa; the founding team came from Blue Origin and SpaceX. Stoke is building Nova, a fully reusable launch vehicle including a reusable upper stage, backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures (Series A) and later large Series C-E rounds, with a 75-acre test site near Moses Lake.
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 Stoke raised a $1bn Series E and unveiled Nova Block 2, a fully reusable medium-lift rocket designed to carry 15 tonnes to low Earth orbit.
notes: Engineering-focused, low public profile (CEO Lapsa is the public face). Web search budget ran out before a sourced personal deep-cut could be found. Stoke publishes only a general info@ inbox.
